messages:
Junaid Patel: heads up — our new quantized runner is showing tiny BERTScore diffs (~0.001-0.004) vs fp16 but the dashboard flags them as regressions. looks like decimal rounding plus our alert threshold is 0.002 :grimacing:
Olga: ugh. are those legit quality drops or metric noise?
Sam: could be numeric nondeterminism from the int8 kernel. we saw that with the attention kernel reorder earlier.
Junaid Patel: I dug in. two things: 1) our BERTScore impl casts floats to float32 then reduces which can flip least-significant bits after quant. 2) the reporting pipeline rounds scores to 3 decimals before plotting which amplifies tiny diffs.
Maria: how are we computing pass@k for the generation tests? might be related if duplicates/ordering changed after quantization.
Junaid Patel: pass@k is the empirical estimator over the sample. but runner changed sample-seed wiring in CI -> examples were sampled in different order, so duplicates ended up in the top-k more often. combined with our dedup postprocess (which is nondeterministic) pass@1 moved by 0.3% on a 10k sample.
Olga: ohhhh seeds. that explains ordering. can we pin the seed in the runner for CI?
Sam: yes — the runner env var SEED was dropped during the caching refactor. quick fix: reintroduce SEED and make sampler deterministic unless RUN_RANDOM=1.
Wes: for BERTScore, we also need consistent tokenization/versioning. are we using the same tokenizer for fp16 vs quant runs?
Junaid Patel: tokenizer is same, but we run a fast-bpe path for quant inference that normalizes unicode slightly differently. fix option: route eval runs through canonical tokenizer path.
Maria: suggestion: change alerting rules to use relative thresholds + p-value test instead of absolute 0.002. small floating noise shouldn't trigger CI.
EvalBot: [eval-runner] job 2063210000: failed quality check — BERTScore delta 0.003 >= threshold 0.002. See logs: https://ci.redwood/exec/2063210000/logs
Sam: proposed action items:
- pin SEED in CI and make sampler deterministic (Sam)
- canonicalize tokenizer for eval-only path (Wes + Junaid)
- change BERTScore aggregation to use float64 reduction before rounding (Junaid)
- relax dashboard alerting to consider both magnitude and sample size (Maria)
Olga: also add a small flakiness test: run metric 3x on the same model/run and assert stdev < epsilon. helps catch nondet kernels.
Junaid Patel: here's a minimal repro snippet I used:
```
# repro for bscore rounding noise
from evals.metrics import bertscore
import numpy as np
refs = ['this is a sentence'] * 1000
hyps_fp16 = refs.copy()
hyps_quant = refs.copy()
hyps_quant[10] = 'this is sentence'  # tiny tokenization diff
s_fp16 = bertscore(hyps_fp16, refs)
s_quant = bertscore(hyps_quant, refs)
print(s_fp16.mean(), s_quant.mean())
```
Sam: perfect. I'll add that to smoke tests.
Maria: can we also log the raw float arrays to S3 for a couple of runs so analytics can compute proper significance?
Wes: yes — add a toggle EVAL_RAW_DUMP=true for nightly runs.
EvalBot: [note] flagged as actionable. created ticket INF-4528 with action items.
Olga: timeline? can we push a hotfix so CI doesn't block merges tonight?
Sam: I'll pin the seed and revert the rounding change in the reporter. small PR in ~30m.
Junaid Patel: thanks all. once PRs are up I'll run the quant vs fp16 smoke matrix and post results here. :thumbsup:
